content: Mater Health Services is a healthcare provider in Brisbane, Australia, offering both public and private medical services. It delivers care to approximately 500,000 patients annually. The organization was founded in 1906 by the Sisters of Mercy. The first Mater Hospital was established in 1906 in a private house called ‘Aubigny’ at North Quay, which was converted into a 20-bed private hospital. By 1911, the revenue generated by the initial Mater Private Hospital and its successor in South Brisbane enabled the Sisters of Mercy to open a free public hospital for the city of Brisbane. In 1931, the Mater Children’s Hospital was inaugurated, treating over 8,266 patients in its first year. The Mater Mothers’ Hospital was officially opened in 1960, providing care for 140 mothers. Key Milestones: In 1919, Queensland’s first hospital laboratory was established at the Mater. In 1928, the Mater Public Hospital installed Queensland’s first deep X-ray therapy machine for cancer treatment. In 1931, the Mater opened the 80-bed Mater Children’s Hospital, the first children’s hospital south of the Brisbane River. In 1954, the Mater established Queensland’s first Neurological Department. Also in 1954, eastern Australia’s first ‘Eye Bank’ was opened at the Mater. In 1967, the first in-utero blood transfusions in Queensland were performed at the Mater. In 1987, the Mater Children’s Hospital established Queensland’s first pediatric sleep unit. In 1989, the Mater Private Priority Emergency Centre was opened, becoming the first of its kind in any Queensland hospital. In 1998, the Mater Children’s Private Hospital was inaugurated, becoming Australia’s first private pediatric facility. In 2000, the Mater Private Hospital—Redland was officially opened. In 2006, Mater Health Services became the first institution to receive a Queensland Greats award.
